subject: Physics
title: Motion: Chapter Introduction
summary: Sitting still? With the Earth you are moving at about 1,500 km/h. Motion is a change of position with time, measured from a reference point, and this chapter gives the tools to describe it.
keyPoints: **Motion** = change of position with time, relative to a **reference point**.
Rest and motion are **relative**: still for the chair, moving for the Sun.
On a distance-time graph: flat = at rest, steeper = faster.

blocks.p: The Earth spins (about **1,500 km/h** at India's latitude) and orbits the Sun (about **1,07,000 km/h**). Whether you are at rest depends on what you compare with.

blocks.alt: A student at rest relative to a chair, but moving with the Earth round the Sun
blocks.caption: Rest for the chair, motion for the Sun.

blocks.alt: A distance-time graph: straight rise, flat while stopped, then steeper
blocks.caption: Flat = stopped; steeper = faster.

quiz.q: An object is in motion when its position:
options: changes with time relative to a reference point
quiz.explain: Motion is a change of position with time, measured from a reference point.

quiz.q: A passenger in a moving train is at rest relative to:
quiz.explain: Her position does not change relative to the train and the people in it.

quiz.q: A flat line on a distance-time graph means the object is:
quiz.explain: The distance is not changing with time.

quiz.q: Which quantity tells how fast velocity changes?
